summary: Feed s183_triple is degraded: 23.3% one-way TCP sessions breaks NDR bidirectional analysis, 9.4% duplicate packets waste capacity, and 91% encrypted bytes exceeds 90% NDR tolerance.

findings.root_cause: 42 of 180 TCP sessions (23.3%) show only one direction, well above 10% threshold. Most likely asymmetric routing where only one side of the conversation is tapped/mirrored, or packet broker is not aggregating both directions of a flow to the same NDR tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions for TCP reassembly, session state tracking and anomaly detection. One-way visibility causes missed detections, incomplete flows, and false positives for scan/connection failures.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow in the packet broker and pin symmetric flows to this NDR port to restore full bidirectional visibility.

findings.root_cause: 260 of 2755 packets (9.4%) are duplicates, above 5% threshold. Typical cause is overlapping SPAN/mirror sources or TAP aggregation without deduplication in the packet broker feeding the same packet twice to the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates inflate NDR flow/packet counters, waste 10G tool capacity and storage, skew analytics and can trigger false duplicate-ACK/retransmission alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets within a short window before delivery to NDR, preserving correct counts without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: 91.4% of bytes are encrypted, just above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is predominantly TLS/encrypted with no decryption visibility, so payload inspection is opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for deep packet inspection and threat detection. With >90% encrypted, detection coverage is severely reduced to metadata only, missing payload-based exploits and C2.

recommended_fix.why: NDR cannot inspect encrypted payload at this share. Advise selective TLS decryption via packet broker / out-of-band decrypt or forwarding decrypted copy from proxy, while respecting privacy policy.
